job_description_info.job_description:
# Backend Engineer (Python) - Shipment Tracking Platform

**Company:** Tessel Cargo Software (FICTIONAL)
**Location:** Antwerp, Belgium (hybrid, 2 days/week in office) – candidates based elsewhere in the EU may work remotely with quarterly on-site weeks
**Employment:** Full-time, permanent
**Team:** Routing & Tracking (7 engineers, 1 engineering manager, 1 product manager)

## About the role

Tessel Cargo Software builds the software that mid-sized freight forwarders use to plan, route and track shipments across Europe. Our Routing & Tracking team owns the services that turn thousands of carrier events per minute into a reliable live picture of where every container, trailer and parcel is.

We are looking for a Backend Engineer with a few years of solid production experience to help us grow this platform. You will work on event ingestion, route-optimisation APIs and the customer-facing tracking API, and you will be on the on-call rota (one week in six, supported by a runbook-driven team).

## What you will do

- Design, build and maintain Python (FastAPI) services that ingest carrier events from EDI, REST webhooks and message queues
- Own parts of our PostgreSQL data model and write migrations that are safe to run on live data
- Improve the performance and reliability of our public tracking API (currently ~400 requests/second at peak)
- Work with the data team to expose clean event streams (Kafka) for analytics and ETA prediction
- Write automated tests, review code and contribute to our CI/CD pipeline (GitHub Actions)
- Help investigate production incidents and write blameless post-mortems
- Take part in architecture discussions and document decisions in short design notes

## What you bring

**Must have**
- 3+ years of professional experience building backend services in Python (or a comparable language such as Go, Java or Kotlin, if you are happy to work mainly in Python)
- Solid experience with relational databases, preferably PostgreSQL, including query tuning and schema migrations
- Experience designing and consuming REST APIs
- Experience with Docker and deploying services to a cloud environment (we use AWS)
- Practical understanding of automated testing and CI/CD
- Good written and spoken English; you can explain technical trade-offs clearly

**Nice to have**
- Experience with Kafka or another event-streaming platform
- Experience with Kubernetes (we run on EKS) and infrastructure as code (Terraform)
- Exposure to observability tooling (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry)
- Knowledge of logistics, transport or supply-chain domains, or EDI formats (EDIFACT, X12)
- Dutch or French language skills

## What we offer

- Salary range EUR 62,000 – 82,000 gross per year depending on experience
- 28 days of holiday, a learning budget of EUR 1,500 per year and a home-office allowance
- Pension scheme, public-transport card and a modern hybrid office near Antwerpen-Centraal
- A team that values pragmatic engineering, clear documentation and sustainable pace

## How to apply

Send us your CV and, if you like, a short cover letter or links to code you are proud of. We read every application and reply within two weeks. Our interviews are: a 30-minute intro call, a practical technical conversation about a past project and a short system-design discussion.

Tessel Cargo Software is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds.

Dear Streamhaus leadership team,

Thank you for the conversations so far about the Director of Engineering, Platform role. I am writing to formally confirm my interest.

Over the past four years as Principal Engineer I have seen the platform from the inside: the entitlement service I designed now handles 120k requests per second, and I led the technical side of the playback API. I believe the next step for the platform is organisational, not only technical. Teams need clear ownership, a lightweight RFC process, and on-call that does not burn people out.

In my first year I would focus on three things: a migration plan for the remaining monolith with clear milestones, a hiring plan to grow the organisation responsibly, and a cost visibility programme so teams understand what their services cost.

I am excited about leading the people I have worked with for years and about building an organisation that keeps engineers close to the code.

With best regards,
Rafael Moretti-Klein

Its tools support more than 340 freight forwarders across 19 countries, placing the company at the intersection of software, freight, and supply-chain operations.

Tessel’s stated values are **“Be dependable. Say what you see. Leave it better.”** Its culture emphasizes practical ownership: small product teams build and operate their services, engineers take part in on-call support, and teams reserve time for reliability work. The company favors concise design notes, invests in observability, and shares technical knowledge through an engineering blog and local Python meetup. It has offices in Antwerp and Poznań, alongside a remote-first engineering group, and is expanding its engineering team and tracking capabilities.

## Tessel Cargo Software raises EUR 24 million to expand live tracking across Europe
**Antwerp, 12 March 2026**

Tessel Cargo Software, the Antwerp-based provider of routing and tracking software for freight forwarders, announced a EUR 24 million Series B round. The funding will be used to double the engineering team by the end of 2027, extend the Tessel Track API with predictive ETAs and open a second engineering hub in Poznań.

"Forwarders still lose hours every day to chasing status updates," said co-founder and CEO Margot Vandenberg. "Our goal is that a dispatcher never has to phone a driver to ask where a trailer is."

CTO Piotr Lis said the company is migrating its event pipeline from queue-based workers to Kafka streams to support peak loads during the autumn peak season, and is investing in observability and on-call tooling. "We want engineers who enjoy running the things they build," he added.

Tessel says it processed 38 million shipment events per day in February 2026, up 2.4x from a year earlier, and that its tracking API maintained 99.95% availability over the last twelve months.

cover_letter_history.content:
Dear Tessel Cargo Software team,

I am applying for the Backend Engineer (Python) role to bring my experience building reliable backend services and distributed systems to your shipment tracking platform. After leading platform engineering at Streamhaus, I am looking to return to a hands-on individual contributor role, working close to the code and the services I help build.

At Streamhaus, I designed and wrote most of a Go entitlement service that handled 120,000 requests per second at peak, and served as technical lead for the playback API. I also helped migrate a Python monolith into approximately 60 Python and Go services, improving playback API availability from 99.5% to 99.95%. This work involved service design, production reliability, and clear technical decisions across a large distributed platform. Earlier, I built backend services that ingested GPS data from 300,000 vehicles for a fleet-telematics platform, an experience directly relevant to tracking and transport systems.

I would bring substantial Python backend experience with FastAPI and Tornado, PostgreSQL/PostGIS and message-oriented systems, Kafka, and production observability with Prometheus, Grafana, and OpenTelemetry. I have also worked with Kubernetes and Terraform when deploying and operating services on GKE. I also bring practical automated-testing experience, including a Python test harness used by QA for eight years. At Streamhaus, I introduced an RFC process, architecture reviews, and on-call guidelines adopted company-wide. Tessel’s emphasis on practical ownership, concise design notes, and a sustainable approach to reliability particularly appeals to me.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience could contribute to the Routing & Tracking team. Thank you for your consideration.

With best regards,
Rafael Moretti-Klein

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is concise, professional, and well tailored to Tessel Cargo Software’s shipment-tracking context. It presents strong quantified evidence: 120,000 requests per second, approximately 60 services, improved availability from 99.5% to 99.95%, and ingestion from 300,000 vehicles. The transition from engineering leadership back to an individual-contributor role is explained clearly and credibly. The letter also connects the candidate’s fleet-telematics experience to logistics and transport systems, which is particularly relevant. A few phrases are broad or slightly imprecise, especially the long technology list and “message-oriented systems.” The letter could also make the Python focus more prominent given the role title and the candidate’s stated interest in hands-on backend work.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document is highly readable and ATS-safe: standard headings are unnecessary in a short letter, the prose uses conventional paragraphs, and the employer, role title, Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Kafka, Kubernetes, Terraform, automated testing, Prometheus, Grafana, and OpenTelemetry keywords are present. Its likely AI/ATS screening probability is good because it contains relevant technologies, quantified backend outcomes, logistics-related experience, and clear alignment with reliability and technical documentation. However, it does not explicitly include several advertised terms that are not substantiated in the candidate material: Docker, CI/CD, REST APIs, PostgreSQL query tuning, and schema migrations. Those should not be added without evidence. The technology list in the third paragraph could be made easier to parse by using more direct, standard wording and separating Python, databases, messaging, deployment, and testing experience.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The letter aligns strongly with the role’s backend, Python, distributed-systems, reliability, observability, Kafka, Kubernetes, Terraform, automated-testing, architecture-discussion, and logistics-domain themes. The fleet-telematics work is a particularly convincing connection to shipment tracking and transport systems. The candidate clearly meets the experience threshold and demonstrates fluent English through the letter itself. The candidate’s material does not establish Docker experience, REST API experience specifically, PostgreSQL query tuning, schema migrations, CI/CD, or Dutch/French language skills. These are genuine profile gaps or unverified requirements rather than defects that should be solved by unsupported wording. The letter appropriately avoids claiming AWS depth, EDI experience, or direct shipment-tracking experience.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the opening paragraph, make the Python focus more explicit. Change “I am applying for the Backend Engineer (Python) role to bring my experience building reliable backend services and distributed systems to your shipment tracking platform” to “I am applying for the Backend Engineer (Python) role to bring my production experience building Python backend services and distributed systems to Tessel’s shipment-tracking platform.” This foregrounds the principal screening keyword without overstating the candidate’s experience.

2. In the third paragraph, replace the broad and slightly awkward technology-list sentence beginning “I would bring substantial Python backend experience...” with more precise wording: “My backend experience includes Python with FastAPI and Tornado, PostgreSQL/PostGIS, Cassandra, Kafka, RabbitMQ, Kubernetes, Terraform, and production observability with Prometheus, Grafana, and OpenTelemetry.” This improves readability and ATS parsing while retaining only technologies supported by the candidate information.

3. In the second paragraph, strengthen the logistics connection without claiming shipment-tracking experience. Change “an experience directly relevant to tracking and transport systems” to “experience directly relevant to event ingestion and transport-data systems.” This more closely reflects the documented GPS-ingestion work and avoids implying that the candidate previously built shipment-tracking software.

4. In the third paragraph, change “I also bring practical automated-testing experience” to “I also bring practical automated-testing experience and production-quality practices, including a Python test harness used by QA for eight years.” This keeps the testing claim grounded in the source material and gives it slightly more impact. Do not add CI/CD, Docker, REST, query tuning, or schema-migration claims unless the candidate can substantiate them.
